newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. asks for federal disaster aid.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. asks for federal disaster aid.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson declared a state of emergency Friday in 12 more counties due to floods and asked President Clinton to issue a federal disaster declaration for 37 storm-ravaged counties.
"This incident is of such severity and magnitude that effective response and recovery is beyond the capabilities of the state and local governments," Wilson wrote in a letter to Clinton.
"In addition, due to the massive numbers of individuals being evacuated, direct federal assistance is necessary for mass care," Wilson wrote.

Wilson proclaimed a state of emergency in 12 more counties in northern and central California, in addition to the 25 counties where he declared an emergency on Thursday. More than half of California's 58 counties are now covered by the emergency proclamation.
A week of fierce storms caused flooding in many parts of northern and central California, causing widespread damage.
Wilson also requested an initial disaster recovery grant of $25 million from the U.S. Department of Labor to create temporary jobs for unemployed people to help in the storm cleanup.
